findings.summary: In _fetch_tweet, `author: "{tweet_author}"` interpolates the oEmbed API's `author_name` field into a quoted YAML scalar without calling `_yaml_str()`, unlike every sibling field in the same hunk (source_url and contributor both got `_yaml_str()` wrapping). `tweet_author` is fetched metadata (`data.get("author_name", "unknown")` from publish.twitter.com's response) — exactly the class of value the brief says must be escaped. A value such as `x"\ncontributor: "hacked"\nadmin: true` breaks out of the quoted scalar and injects arbitrary frontmatter keys, reproducing the exact vulnerability the task asked to close. This is visible directly in the diff: the `-author: {tweet_author}` / `+author: "{tweet_author}"` hunk only adds quotes, not escaping.

findings.summary: The implementer's report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff touches only graphify/export.py and graphify/ingest.py — tests/test_ingest.py and tests/test_export.py are unmodified and no new test file was added. There is no automated coverage asserting that fetched title/author/contributor values are YAML-escaped in frontmatter, nor that </script> sequences in labels are escaped in the HTML export. Such a test would have caught the unescaped `tweet_author` field above.
